claims.claim: UC1 Install coyomap into a coding agent: Someone who has cloned this project asks to install it. Their coding agent gains a new command, and the tools it drives are built and ready.
claims.why_risky: the headline sentence of the behavioural layer — a reader takes the trigger and the outcome away as what the product does.

claims.claim: UC2 Build a project's first map: A person asks their coding agent for a map of a project that has none. A map of that project exists, pinned to the commit it describes.
claims.why_risky: the headline sentence of the behavioural layer — a reader takes the trigger and the outcome away as what the product does.

claims.claim: UC3 Leave code off the map: A person names committed code the map is not meant to describe. Later maps leave that code out, and every count the tools print says so.
claims.why_risky: the headline sentence of the behavioural layer — a reader takes the trigger and the outcome away as what the product does.

claims.claim: UC4 Serve the maps on this machine: A person starts the local map server. Every project they have mapped is listed on one page in their browser.
claims.why_risky: the headline sentence of the behavioural layer — a reader takes the trigger and the outcome away as what the product does.

claims.claim: UC5 Explore a project's map: A person opens a project's map. They see what the product does and drill from one feature down to a single box.
claims.why_risky: the headline sentence of the behavioural layer — a reader takes the trigger and the outcome away as what the product does.

claims.claim: UC6 Open the code behind a box: A reader picks the code link on a box. The file opens at that line, in their own editor or on the code host.
claims.why_risky: the headline sentence of the behavioural layer — a reader takes the trigger and the outcome away as what the product does.

claims.claim: UC7 See what a code change did to the map: The code has moved on since the map was pinned. A report names the parts of the map the change touched.
claims.why_risky: the headline sentence of the behavioural layer — a reader takes the trigger and the outcome away as what the product does.

claims.claim: UC8 Fold a change report into the baseline: A person agrees the change report is right. The map is edited to match, re-pinned, and checked again.
claims.why_risky: the headline sentence of the behavioural layer — a reader takes the trigger and the outcome away as what the product does.

claims.claim: UC9 Change the map by asking: A person asks in plain language for a part of the map to move, split or be renamed. The map is edited in place and passes its checks.
claims.why_risky: the headline sentence of the behavioural layer — a reader takes the trigger and the outcome away as what the product does.

claims.claim: UC10 Score whether the method got better: Someone changed the instructions and wants to know the cost. Two maps of one project are scored and compared, with a verdict.
claims.why_risky: the headline sentence of the behavioural layer — a reader takes the trigger and the outcome away as what the product does.

claims.claim: UC11 Review a finished build: A build has finished and its chat is on disk. A report names the friction, the bugs and the gaps that run revealed.
claims.why_risky: the headline sentence of the behavioural layer — a reader takes the trigger and the outcome away as what the product does.
